isva-p01-v01.speaker: Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)
isva-p01-v01.question: Under what auspice does the Lord's proof open?
premises: He who makes (karoti) — him (tam), I (aham) praise (naumi): the one (ekam) God (devam), Maheśvara the Lord.
The auspice names the conclusion in advance: maker, one, Lord.
isva-p01-v01.inference: Auspice: praise of the one maker-Lord whose proof follows.
uncertainties: Opening pādas lost to print lacuna; the surviving half-verse is complete as praise.

isva-p01-v02.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v02.question: What is the inference to be proved?
premises: Bodies and the rest (tanvādi) have conscious cause (buddhimaddhetu), having distinct arrangement (saṃniveśaviśeṣavat).
Like pots (ghaṭa ... like atoms, paramāṇuvat — mid-verse lacuna).
The Nyāya shape is unmistakable: pakṣa (bodies), hetu (arrangement), dṛṣṭānta (pot).
isva-p01-v02.inference: Thesis stated in Nyāya dress: arranged bodies bespeak a conscious maker, like pots.
uncertainties: Mid-verse gap (dots) eats the example's middle; atoms-vs-pot pairing partly lost — read with prose.

isva-p01-v03.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v03.question: What survives of the example's turn?
premises: Urged by the conscious (buddhimat-prorito) — or (vā) ... [lacuna].
Remnant ṭato ([ta]ṭo? — thence?) — pot (ghaṭaḥ), as (yathā).
The yathā-form survives: 'as pot from [tha]t' — example-phrase intact.
isva-p01-v03.inference: Fragment: the example-form (as pot...) survives its verse.
uncertainties: Major lacuna; prorito unattested (pra+√īr?); ṭato unresolved. No doctrine built on remnants.

isva-p01-v04.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v04.question: What survives of the fixed-meaning turn?
premises: ... without arrangement ([saṃ]skāra-saṃsthāna-varjitaḥ?).
Fixed (niścitaḥ) is its meaning (arthaḥ) in locus (saṃsthāne) — in that (tasmin), action-heaped (arthakriyā) ... (cite remnant).
isva-p01-v04.inference: Fragment: fixed meaning in its locus, amid action-heaping.
uncertainties: Leading lacuna; cite isolated (vocative of cita? severed compound?). Held open.

isva-p01-v05.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v05.question: How is the maker marked?
premises: In the varied (vicitre), the conscious alone (buddhimān eva) is marked (lakṣyate) — as among pots (ghaṭādiṣv iva).
The maker (kartā), wise (vijñaḥ), having resolve for varied-this-use (vicitraitadupayogābhisaṃdhimān).
Prose: variety (vaicitrya) is the mark editors of Nyāya-examples read for intelligence.
isva-p01-v05.inference: Variety marks the wise maker: resolved on varied use, visible among pots.

isva-p01-v06.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v06.question: Can matter arrange?
premises: There is (asti), in function-yoking (arthakriyāyoge), among bodies and worlds (śarīrabhuvanādiṣu).
This distinct arrangement (ayam saṃniveśaviśeṣaḥ) — not possibly from material (anupādānasaṃbhavī).
isva-p01-v06.inference: Arrangement in function-fit things cannot come from matter alone.

isva-p01-v07.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v07.question: What follows from proved makers?
premises: Then here (tat atra), by proving conscious makers (buddhimatkartṛsiddhyā), Lord-action is proved (siddheśvarakriyā).
For knowers of such variety (tādṛśavaicitryaviduṣaḥ), non-lordliness (anīśitā) is impossible (syāt = would be — denied).
isva-p01-v07.inference: Makers proved prove the Lord's act: variety-knowers cannot be lordless.

isva-p01-v08.speaker: Objector (Nyāya-Buddhist voice; cf. anvaya debates)
isva-p01-v08.question: Does concomitance hold for potter or Lord?
premises: Neither by potter (kulālena) nor by Lord (īśena) is agreement (anvayaḥ) shown here (atra).
Since (yatas) for him there would be either opposition (viruddhatā) or unproved agreement (asiddhānvayatā).
Prose: the stock Nyāya worry — anvaya with an unseen maker is unproved; with a seen one, off-point.
isva-p01-v08.inference: Objection stated: the concomitance fails on both horns — opposition or unprovedness.
uncertainties: Voice attribution (objection vs concession) from prose context; the reply (v09) confirms objector.

isva-p01-v09.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p01-v09.question: What answers the anvaya dilemma?
premises: Merely (kevalam) even from showing (saṃdarśanāt) pervasion (vyāpti) with the conscious alone (buddhimanmātra).
By thesis-property force (pakṣadharmabalāt), somewhere (kvacit), someone (kaścit) wise (dhīmān) is understood (pratīyate).
isva-p01-v09.inference: Reply: bare showing of conscious-only pervasion suffices — by pakṣadharma-force alone, some wise one is grasped. Minimalism against the dilemma.

isva-p02-v10.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v10.question: How is the higher self shown in eye etc.?
premises: As (yathā) combination-ness (saṃghātatva) is seen (anvitekṣite) merely for another's sake (pārārthyamātreṇa).
In eye etc. (cakṣurādau), by that fitness (tadaucityāt): the self-dear (ātmeṣṭaḥ), uncompounded (asaṃhataḥ), higher (paraḥ).
Prose: Sāṅkhya's own eye-example turned — fitness, not assemblage, shows the self-cherished uncompounded.
isva-p02-v10.inference: The higher self shows in eye etc. by fitness, as combination seen for another's sake.

isva-p02-v11.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v11.question: How is fire proved as khadira-wood?
premises: As (yathā) from afar (dūrataḥ), from smoke (dhūmāt), proving (siddhiḥ) in a khadira-grove (khadirakānane).
Fire (vahniḥ) is proved (siddhyati) just by knowing it (tatpratipattyā), as khadira-wood (khādiratvena).
Stock smoke-fire example redeployed: mere knowing-it suffices for wood-kind — no need to see the logs.
isva-p02-v11.inference: Fire is proved as khadira-wood by mere knowing: the stock example turned for fitness.

isva-p02-v12.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v12.question: What is the hetu, and what is excluded?
premises: Thus (evam) the cause (hetuḥ): locus-form alone (saṃsthānamātram), here (atra) distinguished (viśeṣitam).
Not (na) by variety merely (vaicitryamātreṇa) as svalakṣaṇa-mark (svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā).
Prose: against the Buddhist svalakṣaṇa-only mark — bare variety doesn't mark; the hetu is fenced.
isva-p02-v12.inference: The hetu stated (locus-form alone) and fenced: not bare variety as particular-mark.
uncertainties: svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā scope (whose mark?) from prose — read as the Buddhist's mark, refused.

isva-p02-v13.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v13.question: What do others sift?
premises: By others too (paraiḥ taiḥ api), of reasons (hetūnāṃ), in pot-self-sifting (ghaṭātmapravivecane).
Locus-form alone (saṃsthānamātram) ... even (eva) ... [gap] ... causehood (hetutvam) of the conscious-possessor (buddhiśālinaḥ).
isva-p02-v13.inference: Others too sift reasons in pot-self-analysis: bare locus-form [carries] the conscious one's causehood.
uncertainties: Mid-verse gap (eva…); the carried predicate partly lost — read with prose, nothing restored.

isva-p02-v14.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v14.question: What whole is rightly Lord-made?
premises: Mutual-function-fit-locus-formed (anyonyārthakriyāyogyasaṃniveśaviśeṣitam) — that (tat), this (idam) whole (sakalam) world (viśvam).
Rightly (yuktam) Lord-made (īśvaranirmitam).
isva-p02-v14.inference: The mutual-fit world-whole is rightly Lord-made.

isva-p02-v15.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v15.question: What strange way of helpers?
premises: Here it is replied (atrocyate): a strange way (gatiścitrā) of helpers (sahakāriṇām) is seen (dṛśyate).
Some (kecit) somehow (kathaṃcid) would join (eveyuḥ) with materials (upādānaiḥ) — a joining (samāgamam).
Metrically confirmed v15ab (8+8); atrocyate kept as verse-opening reply-formula.
isva-p02-v15.inference: Reply-frame opened: helpers show a strange way — some joining with materials somehow.

isva-p02-v16.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v16.question: How do helpers picture effects?
premises: Helpers (hetumantaḥ), entering (praviśya) as others (anye), reaching (prāpya) material-form (upādānarūpatām).
They picture (citrayanti) effects (kāryāṇi) — like earth-water-juices (bhaumodakarasā iva).
isva-p02-v16.inference: Helpers picture effects by entering-as-other and reaching material-form — like earth-juices.

isva-p02-v17.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v17.question: Are outward-changers capable?
premises: Others (anye), again (punar), in material (upādāne), outward-changing (bahirviparivartinaḥ).
For form-variety-yoking (rūpavaicitryayogāya) in effects (kāryeṣu) — not so (na tathā) capable (kṣamāḥ).
isva-p02-v17.inference: Outward-changers in matter can't yoke form-variety in effects.

isva-p02-v18.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p02-v18.question: Does imagined spread order all?
premises: There (tatra), if (yadi) the conscious one's spread (prasaraḥ) by name (nāma) be imagined (kalpyate).
Not (na) by that much alone (tāvataiva) does order (vyavasthā) hold everywhere (sarvatra) — thus (tathā ghaṭate).
isva-p02-v18.inference: Imagined spread of the conscious doesn't alone order everywhere.

isva-p03-v19.speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
isva-p03-v19.question: How is pradhāna proved?
premises: There is (asti), of this proved (prasiddhasya) pradhāna (pradhānasya), by anvaya and the rest (anvayādinā).
By denial (niṣedhena) of self-aims and the like (svārthatādi), person-aim-ness (puruṣārthatā) is proved (sādhitā).
Prose: Sāṅkhya's satkārya/anvaya apparatus — pradhāna established through concomitance, purposed to spirit.
isva-p03-v19.inference: Sāṅkhya stated: pradhāna proved by anvaya; purposed to spirit by denying self-aims.

isva-p03-v20.speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
isva-p03-v20.question: How easy is change?
premises: Through that (tena), person's (puruṣasya) enjoyment-proving (bhogasaṃsiddhiḥ) — again and again (yathā yathā).
So (tathā tathā), change (pariṇatiḥ) would be (syāt) nothing (na kiṃcana) hard (durghaṭam).
isva-p03-v20.inference: Change comes easy, again and again, for spirit's enjoyment.

isva-p03-v21.speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
isva-p03-v21.question: What moves pradhāna?
premises: Hence indeed (ata eva), for ever-becoming (mahattvapariṇāminaḥ) pradhāna (pradhānasya).
No (na) nimitta-cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ) other (anyat) but (ṛte) person-aim-striving (puruṣārthodyamāt).

isva-p03-v22.speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
isva-p03-v22.question: What is own-nature for?
premises: Own-nature (svabhāvaḥ) indeed (eva) — and (ca) this (eṣaḥ) of this (asya).
From seeing the root-cause then (mūlahetoḥ tatekṣaṇāt); below mind-ground (cittabhūmer adharataḥ), toward body-ordaining (śarīrādi vidhim).
isva-p03-v22.inference: Own-nature faces downward: from root-cause-seeing toward body's ordaining.
uncertainties: tatekṣaṇāt parsed then-seeing (tat+ekṣaṇāt); at-the-moment (tate+kṣaṇāt) equivalent in force — settled.

isva-p03-v23.speaker: Sāṅkhya closing / siddhāntin opening (pivot)
question: As efficient cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ), karma (karma) could be (syāt) even (api) original-natured (ādya-svabhāvataḥ).
Then (tatas) here (atra) — where (kutra) is Īśvara's business (vyāpāraḥ) to be conceived (upakalpyatām)?
Prose: karma-as-nimitta considered and bounded; the question turns the page.
premises: As efficient cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ), karma (karma) could be (syāt) even (api) original-natured (ādya-svabhāvataḥ).
Then (tatas) here (atra) — where (kutra) is Īśvara's business (vyāpāraḥ) to be conceived (upakalpyatām)?
Prose: karma-as-nimitta considered and bounded; the question turns the page.
isva-p03-v23.inference: Pivot: karma admitted as possible nimitta — then where is Īśvara's business?
uncertainties: v23cd read as siddhāntin's programmatic question (answered v24); Sāṅkhya-dismissal reading recorded but set aside — see NOTE.

isva-p03-v24.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p03-v24.question: What is to be conceived?
premises: Of secret nature (rahanatvasya — print's (natva) kept), in root-nature (mūlaprakṛtau), protecting (avantaḥ) inner-organ-rangers (karaṇacāriṇaḥ).
Let Īśvara's (īśvarasya) change-causality (pariṇāmanimittatā) be conceived (upakalpyeta).
isva-p03-v24.inference: Proposal: let Īśvara's change-causality be conceived for root-nature's rangers.
uncertainties: rahanatvasya unresolved (rahaḥ? rahana? + natva?) — kept as printed with insertion; sense from prose. Held open.

isva-p03-v25.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p03-v25.question: What example?
premises: If (yadi) of uniform-change-nature (pariṇāmaikasvabhāvaṃ) — then (atha) thence (tataḥ).
Independent (ananyāpekṣi) seed-kitchen (bījādisāmagrī), as (yadvat) in sprout (aṅkure).
isva-p03-v25.inference: Seed-kitchen example: independent, as in sprouts.

isva-p03-v26.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p03-v26.question: What of Sāṅkhya?
premises: The mahad-first-change-torrent-natured (mahadādivikāraughapariṇāmasvabhāvakam), three-natured (triguṇātma) pradhāna-self (pradhānaṃ).
And (ca) thereby (tena): godless (anīśvaram) Sāṅkhya (sāṃkhyam).
isva-p03-v26.inference: Verdict on Sāṅkhya: three-natured pradhāna — thereby godless.

isva-p03-v27.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p03-v27.question: What is conceived?
premises: If (cet) puruṣārtha-natured (puruṣārthasvabhāvatvaṃ) in all function-acts (samastārthakriyāsu).
By pradhāna (pradhānasya) it is conceived (upakalpyate) as efficient (nimittakāraṇatvena).
isva-p03-v27.inference: Conditional close: puruṣārtha-natured acts conceived efficient by pradhāna.

isva-p04-v28.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v28.question: Without what no pot?
premises: Without that (tat vinā) — without potter (kumbhakāreṇa) — even a pot (ghaṭo'pi).
How (katham) could it be (bhavet)?
isva-p04-v28.inference: No pot without potter: how else could it be?

isva-p04-v29.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v29.question: What of clay-lump nature?
premises: From the pradhāna-made clay-lump (pradhānamayamṛtpiṇḍāt) indeed (eva) — of such nature (tādṛksvabhāvataḥ).
Now (atha): own-nature (svabhāvaḥ) — this (eṣaḥ) of this (asya) — which (yat) looks to potter and the rest (kulālādi apekṣaṇam).
isva-p04-v29.inference: Own-nature looks to potter etc.: clay-lump nature potter-watching.

isva-p04-v30.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v30.question: Can helpers entering matter arrange?
premises: Not (na) indeed (eva): by entering (praveśāt) inside the material cause (upādānahetvantaḥ), with helpers (sahakāribhiḥ).
Arrangement (saṃniveśaḥ) could (śakyaḥ) be made (kartum), they say (iti) — though able (kṣamam).
Prose: entering doesn't transfer arrangement-making; helpers stay helpers.
isva-p04-v30.inference: Entering matter with helpers can't make arrangement — ability aside.

isva-p04-v31.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v31.question: Without what wisdom?
premises: World-traffic-linking-having (lokayātrānusaṃdhānavatīṃ) wisdom (prajñāṃ) — without (vinā) — not indeed (nahi).
isva-p04-v31.inference: Hemistich as printed: without world-linked wisdom — never.
uncertainties: Hemistich (cd lost in print); nothing restored.

isva-p04-v32.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v32.question: Without desiring?
premises: So (tathā), without (vinā) desiring-to-make (cikīrṣāṃ), no wondrous-making arising (vicitraracanodbhavaḥ).
There'd be mere grossness (sthūlatāmātram), not (na) world-useful (lokopayoginī) — but (tu).
isva-p04-v32.inference: No will, no wonders: mere grossness, never world-good.

isva-p04-v33.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v33.question: If from potter-helping?
premises: Making (racanā) by rule (niyamena) would be (syāt) wondrous (vicitrā), kind-formed (jātirūpiṇī).
If (cet) from potter-helping-mereness (kulālasahakāritvamātrāt) a pot is born (jāyate ghaṭaḥ).
isva-p04-v33.inference: Conditional: rule-wondrous making — if mere potter-help bore pots.

isva-p04-v34.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v34.question: What of bodies and arrangement?
premises: Never (na) would there be (syāt) body etc. (śarīrādi) — long clay-lump (dīrghamṛtpiṇḍa) or (vā).
Hence (atas) indeed (eva): by being-led-to-the-end (arthanīyatvāt), arrangement (saṃniveśaḥ) excels (viśiṣyate).
isva-p04-v34.inference: No bodies otherwise; end-led arrangement excels.

isva-p04-v35.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v35.question: Lord or non-Lord?
premises: Not (na) by pot-etc.-ness (ghaṭāditayā) proved (siddhaḥ) — the need-fulfiller (arthitāparipūrakaḥ).
Neither Lord (īśvaraḥ) nor non-Lord (anīśvaraḥ) is taken (prakṛtaḥ) here (atra) as atomic-marked (aṇulakṣaṇaḥ).
isva-p04-v35.inference: Both extremes fenced: neither Lord nor un-Lord atomically taken.

isva-p04-v36.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p04-v36.question: Does pradhāna will?
premises: Nor (na) of pradhāna (pradhānasya) desire-etc.-arising (icchādi saṃbhavaḥ)...
person-aim-ness (puruṣārthatā).
uncertainties: na-scope ambiguous (denies arising? or denies puruṣārthatā?); read as fencing will off pradhāna, keeping puruṣārthatā — held open.

isva-p05-v37.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p05-v37.question: Unperceived arising — whose purpose?
premises: Buddhi's arising-or-not (saṃbhavan apy asaṃbhavī).
Without spirit-perceptibility (vinā saṃvedyatāṃ puṃsaḥ).
In such a state (tathātve).
isva-p05-v37.inference: No puruṣārthatā where no spirit perceives (sentence completes in v38).
uncertainties: Cross-verse sentence: bare puruṣārthatā completes in v38's avācyā — read together.

isva-p05-v38.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p05-v38.question: Unspeakable — of whom?
premises: Even of spirit, even of pradhāna — unspeakable (puṃso'pi syāt pradhānasyāvācyā).
Of the mere (kevalasya tu).
Yet mind's/buddhi's function is individually conditioned (athāpi manaso vṛttir buddher vā ekaikasaṃskṛtā).
isva-p05-v38.inference: Denial stands; the concession is the objector's best case, pressed in v39.
uncertainties: cd concedes the objector's best case (individual conditioning) to press it in v39.

isva-p05-v39.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p05-v39.question: How could will serve all?
premises: Will, indeed — how serve all spirits' purposes (icchā nāma kathaṃ sarvapuruṣārthopayoginī syāt)?
The escape: it belongs to generic pradhāna, for all (kiṃ tu sā pradhānasya sāmānyasya akhilān prati).
isva-p05-v39.inference: The how-question marks the generic-will escape, demolished in v40.
uncertainties: kiṃ-tu pivots to the generic-pradhāna escape, demolished in v40.

isva-p05-v40.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p05-v40.question: Perceived — by whom?
premises: Even unperceived by spirit, could it be? Not will (puṃso'pi syāt…asaṃvedyā na…icchā).
Perceived — by whom would it be (vedyā ca kasya sā)?
If by all: omniscience of each follows (yadi sarveṣāṃ sārvajñyam ekaikasya prasajyate).
isva-p05-v40.inference: Generic will forces omniscience on each — reductio.

isva-p05-v41.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin, voicing the escape)
isva-p05-v41.question: One light — whose divisions?
premises: Through light-unity the distinct appearances would mix (saṃkīryeran prakāśaikyāt bhinnāś cābhāsamānatāḥ).
The escape: by some One undivided from all spirits (athāpi sarvapuruṣābhinnena ekena kenacit).
isva-p05-v41.inference: The escape becomes the Īśvara-turn (prose: tatsa eveśvaro'stu).
uncertainties: cd — the objector's escape that becomes the Īśvara-turn; voice held as siddhāntin-voiced.

isva-p05-v42.speaker: Pūrvapakṣin (svabhāva-vādin)
isva-p05-v42.question: Seed to sprout — by what purpose?
premises: Not from world-sustenance-purpose would it produce seed into sprout (na lokayātrābhiprāyāt janayed bījam aṅkuram).
But by nature — such a kit is its cause, of such a kind (kiṃ tu svabhāvāt sā tasya sāmagrī hetur īdṛśaḥ).
isva-p05-v42.inference: Nature's kit suffices — the svabhāva position stated.

isva-p05-v43.speaker: Pūrvapakṣin (svabhāva-vādin)
isva-p05-v43.question: Purpose-speech — by what right?
premises: What is born, fit — the wise man joins to one another (yaj jātaṃ yogyam anyonyaṃ yojayed buddhimāñ janaḥ).
By this courtesy, puruṣārthatva is said of it (asya tena upacāreṇa puruṣārthatvam ucyate).
isva-p05-v43.inference: Purpose is courtesy-speech — the thread v44 pulls.
uncertainties: upacāra-concession: puruṣārthatva merely metaphorical — the thread pulled in v44.

isva-p05-v44.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p05-v44.question: Granted — then what, for the freed?
premises: If thus (iti cet).
Even on completion, even in purpose (tat samāptau api puruṣārthe api).
Toward him — the freed spirit (taṃ prati).
isva-p05-v44.inference: The grant suspends; the blow lands in v45.
uncertainties: Protasis suspends; apodosis lands in v45.

isva-p05-v45.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p05-v45.question: Ceaseless churning — whose liberation?
premises: From own-effect-change the root-cause would not cease (svakāryapariṇāmāt na viramen mūlakāraṇam).
Oh — it does not cease (āho na viramati).
This beyond, in nature's seven (etat paraṃ prakṛtisaptake).
isva-p05-v45.inference: Nature-alone never releases — hence a perceiving maker (v52).
uncertainties: āho ironic — the objector's triumph voiced to collapse it; drives to v52's buddhimatkartṛ.

isva-p06-v46.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v46.question: Desired by all — yet whose change?
premises: From change, that One is desired for all spirits (pariṇāmāt tad ekaṃ hi sarvān puṃsaḥ pratīṣyate).
Yet body-earth-and-rest's change is by nature (tathāpi dehabhūtādeḥ pariṇāmaḥ svabhāvataḥ).
isva-p06-v46.inference: The grant (all desire the One) pressed by the body-case.
uncertainties: taye pāṭhāntara for tathāpi in apparatus — sense stable under either; print reading kept.

isva-p06-v47.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v47.question: Why not for the deemed-freed?
premises: As before — why would it not be, toward the deemed-freed (pūrvavan na bhavet kasmāt taṃ muktābhimataṃ prati)?
Yet it does occur — but is not joined by him (athāpi sa bhavaty eva kiṃ tu tena na yujyate).
isva-p06-v47.inference: Occurrence without union — the freed-spirit test.

isva-p06-v48.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v48.question: Needlessness — whose?
premises: By the freed spirit — done with tasks, need-free — he stands alone (mukta-puṃsā kṛtārthatvād anarthitvāt sa kevalaḥ).
Not so: needlessness belongs to no spirit ever, nor to mind (naitan nārthitvam asyāsti jātu puṃso'tha cetasaḥ).
isva-p06-v48.inference: The objector's need-free spirit denied on both sides.

isva-p06-v49.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v49.question: No reunion — and yet born?
premises: With need gone, no meeting with spirit again would be (arthitvavigamān na syād bhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ).
This too is unjust, once body-dwelling mind is born (tad etad api na nyāyyaṃ jāte dehasthacetasi).

isva-p06-v50.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v50.question: Mokṣa — nature or karma's end?
premises: If from perceptible-only-nature of that, not from karma's waning (saṃvedyaikasvabhāvatvāt tasya karmakṣayān na cet).
Mokṣa would be mere nature, resting on karma's waning (tat svabhāvatvam eva syān mokṣaḥ karmakṣayāśrayaḥ).
isva-p06-v50.inference: The view collapses mokṣa into nature.

isva-p06-v51.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v51.question: Mercy-acts — passionless?
premises: There'd be acts even of spirit-distinction-knowers, from compassion (syur jñātapuṃvivekānāṃ karmāṇy api kṛpāditaḥ).
If not from passion — thus mokṣa from passion's exhaustion (na rāgāt tāni ced evaṃ mokṣo rāgakṣayād bhavet).
isva-p06-v51.inference: Compassion smuggles passion back; the view becomes passion-exhaustion doctrine.

isva-p06-v52.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v52.question: Abandoned — what stands?
premises: Thus view-abandoned — that nature-view is unjust (tathā ca darśanatyāgas tan na yuktā svabhāvadṛk).
Hence body-and-rest, famously, have sentient-maker as prior (tasmāt prasiddhaṃ tanvādi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam).
isva-p06-v52.inference: The siddhānta: bodies bespeak a knowing maker.
uncertainties: svabhāvadṛk agrees with yuktā (the abandoning is nature-viewed).

isva-p06-v53.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v53.question: Proved — by what?
premises: From setup-difference (saṃsthānabhedāt).
This flawless proof (ity etan niravadyaṃ prasādhanam).

isva-p06-v54.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
isva-p06-v54.question: Aimed at whom — shaken by what?
premises: This reason, aimed at the Supreme Lord by the self-entrusted self (sa eṣa hetuḥ parameśvaraṃ prati prayujyamānaḥ svaniveśitātmanā).
Not overpowered by reason-faults in the least (na hetudoṣaiḥ paribhūyate manāk).
Nor the rival's either — only this is said (paro'pi vā kevalam etad ucyate).
isva-p06-v54.inference: The hetu stands aimed at the Lord; rivals answered, disputation closed.
uncertainties: kevalam-etad-ucyate scope: 'only this is said' closes the disputation.

isva-p07-v55.speaker: Utpaladeva (closing)
isva-p07-v55.question: Proved — yet for whom in vain?
premises: Though proved by a thousand blazing reasons (samujjvalan nyāyasahasrasādhito'py upaiti).
It succeeds not for the deluded-minded (siddhiṃ na vimūḍhacetasām).
Maheśvara, placed on the palm, yet flees the fate-struck — the true jewel (maheśvaraḥ pāṇitalasthito'pi san palāyate daivahatasya sanmaṇiḥ).
isva-p07-v55.inference: Proof needs fitness; the jewel flees the fated.

isva-p07-v56.speaker: Utpaladeva (signature)
isva-p07-v56.question: Who shines within — and who signs?
premises: One's own self indeed — this — flashes forth: Īśvara within all breathers (svātmaivāyaṃ sphurati sakalaprāṇinām īśvaro'ntaḥ).
Maker and knower too (kartā jñātāpi ca).
Yet recognition of the beyond is to be effected (yadi paraṃ pratyabhijñāsya sādhyā).
And the joining is made by us elsewhere (sā cāsmābhir vihitaghaṭanānyatra).
But Īśvara-proved stands even in duality (kiṃ tv īśasiddhir dvaite'py asti).
Fitting, and more: fire shines at midnight (ity ucitam adhikaṃ bhāti vahnir niśīthe).
isva-p07-v56.inference: Self is Īśvara within all; the proof stands even dualist; signature and forward glance.
uncertainties: pratyabhijñā-program link: recognition to be effected — the work's forward glance to the Īśvarapratyabhijñā; joining 'made by us elsewhere' points outside this treatise.

isva-p01-v01.plain_english: The maker — him, I praise, the one God, Maheśvara the Lord.

isva-p01-v02.plain_english: Bodies and the rest have conscious cause, distinct-arranged — pots … like atoms.

isva-p01-v04.plain_english: … devoid of locus-form. Fixed is its meaning in place — in that action-heaped …

isva-p01-v05.plain_english: In the varied, the conscious alone is marked — as among pots. The maker, wise, resolved on varied use.
isva-p01-v05.sanskrit_cite: vicitre buddhimāneva ghaṭādiṣviva lakṣyate kartā vijño vicitraitadupayogābhisaṃdhimān

isva-p01-v06.plain_english: There is, in function-yoking, among bodies and worlds, this distinct array — never from mere matter.

isva-p01-v07.plain_english: Here then — conscious makers proved, the Lord's act proved: for such-variety-knowers, lordlessness is impossible.
isva-p01-v07.sanskrit_cite: tadatra buddhimatkartṛsiddhyā siddheśvarakriyā na hi tādṛśavaicitryaviduṣaḥ syādanīśitā

isva-p01-v08.plain_english: Neither potter nor Lord shows agreement here — for him, opposition would follow, or agreement unproved.
isva-p01-v08.sanskrit_cite: na kulālena neśenāpyanvayo'tra pradarśyate yato viruddhatāsya syādasiddhānvayatāpi vā

isva-p01-v09.plain_english: Merely showing pervasion with the conscious alone — by thesis-force, somewhere, someone wise is understood.

isva-p02-v10.plain_english: As combination-ness is seen merely for another's sake — in the eye and the rest, by that fitness: the self-dear, uncompounded higher.
isva-p02-v10.sanskrit_cite: yathā pārārthyamātreṇa saṃghātatve'nvitekṣite cakṣurādau tadaucityādātmeṣṭo'saṃhataḥ paraḥ

isva-p02-v11.plain_english: As from afar, from smoke, proving in a khadira-grove — fire is proved by just knowing it, as khadira-wood.
isva-p02-v11.sanskrit_cite: yathā vā dūrato dhūmātsiddhiḥ khadirakānane vahnistatpratipattyaiva khādiratvena siddhyati

isva-p02-v12.plain_english: Thus the cause: locus-form alone, here distinguished — not by mere variety as svalakṣaṇa-mark.
isva-p02-v12.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca hetuḥ saṃsthānamātramatra viśeṣitam tathā vaicitryamātreṇa na svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā

isva-p02-v13.plain_english: By others too, of reasons, in pot-self-sifting — locus-form alone … even … causehood of the conscious one.
isva-p02-v13.sanskrit_cite: paraistairapi hetūnāṃ ghaṭātmapravivecane saṃsthānamātra eva............ hetutvaṃ buddhiśālinaḥ

isva-p02-v14.plain_english: Mutual-function-fit-locus-formed — that whole world, this — rightly Lord-made.

isva-p02-v15.plain_english: Here is the reply: a strange way of helpers is seen — some would somehow join with materials — a joining.
isva-p02-v15.sanskrit_cite: atrocyate gatiścitrā dṛśyate sahakāriṇām kecitkathaṃcideveyurupādānaiḥ samāgamam

isva-p02-v16.plain_english: Helpers, entering as others, reaching material-form — picture effects indeed — like earth-water-juices.
isva-p02-v16.sanskrit_cite: hetumantaḥpraviśyānye prāpyopādānarūpatām citrayanti hi kāryāṇi bhaumodakarasā iva

isva-p02-v17.plain_english: Others again, in matter, outward-changing — for yoking form-variety in effects, they are not so capable.
isva-p02-v17.sanskrit_cite: anye punarupādāne bahirviparivartinaḥ rūpavaicitryayogāya kāryeṣu na tathā kṣamāḥ

isva-p02-v18.plain_english: There, if the conscious one's spread is imagined in name — not by that alone does order hold everywhere. So it stands.
isva-p02-v18.sanskrit_cite: tatra buddhimato nāma prasaro yadi kalpyate na tāvataiva sarvatra vyavasthā ghaṭate tathā

isva-p03-v19.plain_english: And of this proved pradhāna there is, by anvaya and the rest — by denial of self-aims and the like, person-aim-ness is proved.
isva-p03-v19.sanskrit_cite: asti cāsya pradhānasya prasiddhasyānvayādinā svārthatādiniṣedhena sādhitā puruṣārthatā

isva-p03-v20.plain_english: Through that, person's enjoyment-proving again and again — so change would be nothing hard.
isva-p03-v20.sanskrit_cite: tenāsya bhogasaṃsiddhiḥ puruṣasya yathā yathā tathā tathā pariṇatiḥ syānna kiṃcana durghaṭam

isva-p03-v21.plain_english: Hence indeed, for ever-becoming pradhāna, no efficient cause but person-aim-striving.
isva-p03-v21.sanskrit_cite: ata eva pradhānasya mahattvapariṇāminaḥ nimittakāraṇaṃ nānyatpuruṣārthodyamādṛte

isva-p03-v22.plain_english: Own-nature indeed — and this of this — from seeing the root-cause on; below mind-ground, toward body-ordaining.
isva-p03-v22.sanskrit_cite: svabhāva eva caiṣo'sya mūlahetostathekṣaṇāt cittabhūmeradharataḥ śarīrādividhiṃ prati

isva-p03-v23.plain_english: As efficient cause, karma could be original-natured even. Then here — where is Īśvara's business to be conceived?
isva-p03-v23.sanskrit_cite: nimittakāraṇaṃ karma syādapyādyasvabhāvataḥ tato'tra kutra vyāpāra īśvarasyopakalpyatām

isva-p03-v24.plain_english: Protecting the inner-organ-rangers in root-nature, of secret nature — let Īśvara's change-causality be conceived.

isva-p03-v25.plain_english: If of uniform-change-nature — then thence: independent seed-kitchen, as in sprouts.
isva-p03-v25.sanskrit_cite: yadyathā pariṇāmaikasvabhāvaṃ tatra tattataḥ ananyāpekṣi bījādisāmagrī yadvadaṅkure

isva-p03-v26.plain_english: The mahad-first-change-torrent-natured, three-natured pradhāna-self — thereby godless Sāṅkhya.
isva-p03-v26.sanskrit_cite: mahadādivikāraughapariṇāmasvabhāvakam triguṇātma pradhānaṃ ca tena sāṃkhyamanīśvaram

isva-p03-v27.plain_english: If puruṣārtha-natured in all function-acts — by pradhāna it is conceived as efficient.

isva-p04-v28.plain_english: Without that — how could there be even a pot without a potter?

isva-p04-v29.plain_english: From the pradhāna-made clay-lump indeed, of such nature — now own-nature, this of this, looking to potter and the rest.
isva-p04-v29.sanskrit_cite: pradhānamayamṛtpiṇḍādeva tādṛksvabhāvataḥ atha svabhāva eṣo'sya yatkulālādyapekṣaṇam

isva-p04-v30.plain_english: Not indeed — by entering inside the material cause with helpers — could arrangement be made, says he — capable though they be.
isva-p04-v30.sanskrit_cite: naivopādanahetvantaḥ praveśātsahakāribhiḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣo'pi śakyaḥ kartumiti kṣamam

isva-p04-v32.plain_english: So without desiring-to-make, no wondrous-making arising — there'd be mere grossness, not world-useful.
isva-p04-v32.sanskrit_cite: tathā cikīrṣāṃ ca vinā vicitraracanodbhavaḥ sthūlatāmātrameva syānna tu lokopayoginī

isva-p04-v33.plain_english: Making by rule would be wondrous, kind-formed — if from potter-helping-mereness a pot is born.
isva-p04-v33.sanskrit_cite: racanā niyamena syādvicitrā jātirūpiṇī kulālasahakāritvamātrāccejjāyate ghaṭaḥ

isva-p04-v34.plain_english: Never body etc. — long clay-lump or else — hence arrangement excels by being led to ends.
isva-p04-v34.sanskrit_cite: na syājjātu śarīrādi dīrghamṛtpiṇḍa eva vā ata evārthanīyatvātsaṃniveśo viśiṣyate

isva-p04-v35.plain_english: Not by pot-etc.-ness proved — the need-fulfiller. Neither Lord nor non-Lord is taken here as atomic-marked.
isva-p04-v35.sanskrit_cite: na ghaṭāditayā siddhaḥ so'rthitāparipūrakaḥ na ceśvaro'nīśvaro vā prakṛto'trāṇulakṣaṇaḥ

isva-p05-v37.plain_english: Since intellect's arising, actual or not, stands unperceived by any spirit — puruṣārthatā in such a case [is unspeakable: v38].
isva-p05-v37.sanskrit_cite: yataḥ syādasya buddhestu saṃbhavannapyasaṃbhavī vinā saṃvedyatāṃ puṃsastathātve puruṣārthatā

isva-p05-v38.plain_english: Even of spirit, even of pradhāna, it would be unspeakable — of the mere; yet mind's function, or intellect's, is individually conditioned.
isva-p05-v38.sanskrit_cite: puṃso'pi syātpradhānasyāvācyā sā kevalasya tu athāpi manaso vṛttirbuddhervaikaikasaṃskṛtā

isva-p05-v39.plain_english: Will, indeed — how could it serve all spirits' purposes? But [if] it belongs to generic pradhāna, for all…
isva-p05-v39.sanskrit_cite: icchā nāma kathaṃ sarvapuruṣārthopayoginī syātikiṃ tu sā pradhānasya sāmānyasyākhilānprati

isva-p05-v40.plain_english: Even unperceived by spirit, could it be? Not will — and perceived, by whom would it be? If by all — omniscience of each and every one follows.
isva-p05-v40.sanskrit_cite: puṃsaḥ syātsāpyasaṃvedyā necchā vedyā ca kasya sā sarveṣāṃ yadi sārvajñyamekaikasya prasajyate

isva-p05-v41.plain_english: Through light-unity the distinct appearances would mix; yet [perceived] by some one undivided from all spirits…

isva-p05-v42.plain_english: Not from world-sustenance-purpose would it produce seed into sprout; but by nature — such a kit is its cause, of such a kind.
isva-p05-v42.sanskrit_cite: na lokayātrābhiprāyājjanayedbījamaṅkuram kiṃ tu svabhāvātsā tasya sāmagrī heturīdṛśaḥ

isva-p05-v43.plain_english: What is born, fit — the wise man joins to one another; by this courtesy, puruṣārthatva is spoken of it.
isva-p05-v43.sanskrit_cite: yajjātaṃ yogyamanyonyaṃ yojayedbuddhimāñjanaḥ asya tenopacāreṇa puruṣārthatvamucyate

isva-p05-v44.plain_english: If thus — even on completion, even in purpose, toward him [the freed spirit]…

isva-p05-v45.plain_english: From own-effect-change the root-cause would not cease; oh — it does not cease, this beyond, in the seven of nature.
isva-p05-v45.sanskrit_cite: svakāryapariṇāmānna viramenmūlakāraṇam āho na viramatyetatparaṃ prakṛtisaptake

isva-p06-v46.plain_english: From change, that One is longed for, for all spirits — and yet body's and earth's and the rest's change is by nature.
isva-p06-v46.sanskrit_cite: pariṇāmāttadekaṃ hi sarvānpuṃsaḥ pratīṣyate tathāpi dehabhūtādeḥ pariṇāmaḥ svabhāvataḥ

isva-p06-v47.plain_english: As before — why would it not be, toward the deemed-freed? Yet it does occur — but is not joined by him.
isva-p06-v47.sanskrit_cite: pūrvavanna bhavetkasmāttaṃ muktābhimataṃ prati athāpi sa bhavatyeva kiṃ tu tena na yujyate

isva-p06-v48.plain_english: By the freed spirit — done with tasks, need-free — he stands alone; not so: needlessness belongs to no spirit ever, nor to mind.
isva-p06-v48.sanskrit_cite: muktapuṃsā kṛtārthatvādanarthitvātsa kevalaḥ naitannārthitvamasyāsti jātu puṃso'tha cetasaḥ

isva-p06-v49.plain_english: With need gone, no meeting with spirit again would be; this too is unjust, once body-dwelling mind is born.
isva-p06-v49.sanskrit_cite: arthitvavigamānna syādbhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ tadetadapi na nyāyyaṃ jāte dehasthacetasi

isva-p06-v50.plain_english: If from perceptible-only-nature of that, not from karma's waning — mokṣa would be mere nature, resting on karma's waning.
isva-p06-v50.sanskrit_cite: saṃvedyaikasvabhāvatvāttasya karmakṣayānna cet tatsvabhāvatvameva syānmokṣaḥ karmakṣayāśrayaḥ

isva-p06-v51.plain_english: There'd be acts even of spirit-distinction-knowers, from compassion; if not from passion — thus mokṣa from passion's exhaustion.
isva-p06-v51.sanskrit_cite: syurjñātapuṃvivekānāṃ karmāṇyapi kṛpāditaḥ na rāgāttāni cedevaṃ mokṣo rāgakṣayādbhavet

isva-p06-v52.plain_english: Thus view-abandoned — that nature-view is unjust; hence body-and-rest, famously, have sentient-maker as prior.
isva-p06-v52.sanskrit_cite: tathā ca darśanatyāgastanna yuktā svabhāvadṛk tasmātprasiddhaṃ tanvādi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam

isva-p06-v54.plain_english: This reason, aimed at the Supreme Lord by the self-entrusted self, is not overpowered by reason-faults in the least — nor the rival's either; only this is said.
isva-p06-v54.sanskrit_cite: sa eṣa hetuḥ parameśvaraṃ prati prayujyamānaḥ svaniveśitātmanā na hetudoṣaiḥ paribhūyate manāk paro'pi vā kevalametaducyate

isva-p07-v55.plain_english: Though proved by a thousand blazing reasons, it succeeds not for the deluded-minded; Maheśvara, placed on the palm, yet flees the fate-struck — the true jewel.
isva-p07-v55.sanskrit_cite: samujjvalannyāyasahasrasādhito'pyupaiti siddhiṃ na vimūḍhacetasām maheśvaraḥ pāṇitalasthito'pi san palāyate daivahatasya sanmaṇiḥ

isva-p07-v56.plain_english: One's own self indeed — this — flashes forth: Īśvara within all breathers, maker and knower too; yet recognition of the beyond is to be effected, and the joining is made by us elsewhere. But Īśvara-proved stands even in duality — fitting, and more: fire shines at midnight.
isva-p07-v56.sanskrit_cite: svātmaivāyaṃ sphurati sakalaprāṇināmīśvaro'ntaḥ kartā jñātāpi ca yadi paraṃ pratyabhijñāsya sādhyā sā cāsmābhirvihitaghaṭanānyatra kiṃ tvīśasiddhirdvaite'pyastītyucitamadhikaṃ bhāti vahnirniśīthe

essence: Bodies bespeak a conscious maker, like pots: the design inference stated through lacunae (vv1-2).
Variety marks wisdom; matter can't arrange; makers proved prove the Lord — answering neither-potter-nor-Lord with conscious-only pervasion shown (vv5-9).

sections.SUMMARY: The maker — him praised, one God, Maheśvara. Bodies bespeak conscious cause, distinct-arranged — pots, like atoms. Conscious-urged fragments and fixed-meaning fragments survive around gaps. In the varied, the conscious alone is marked, maker-wise, use-resolved. Function-yoked bodies and worlds hold distinct array, never from mere matter. Makers proved prove the Lord's act; variety-knowers cannot be lordless. Neither potter nor Lord shows agreement — opposition or unprovedness would follow. Merely showing conscious-only pervasion — by thesis-force, some wise one is understood.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as the hetu advances and answers with less
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: the inference stated in full dress, dilemmatized, then answered minimally — bare showing suffices. The vyabhicāri is wonder that less proves more. Nyāya-confidence turned toward a conscious Lord.

essence: Stock examples turned: eye-fitness shows the higher self; smoke-fire proves khadira-wood by mere knowing (vv10-11).
The hetu fenced, others sifting, the whole Lord-made; helpers' strange way opened, pictured, and bounded; fancied spread refused (vv12-18).

sections.SUMMARY: Fitness shows the higher self in eye and the rest, the way combination is seen for another's sake. Fire comes proved as khadira-wood through mere knowing, the way smoke proves from afar. The hetu is fenced to bare locus-form, refusing bare variety the particular's mark. Others sift reasons the same way in the pot's self. The mutual-fit whole stands rightly Lord-made. Helpers answer strangely — some joining with stuff — picturing effects by entering-as-other, like earth-saps. Outward-turned others cannot yoke form-variety. Fancied spread, named but unshown, orders nothing alone.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as each stock case turns to show fitness
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: eye, fire, pot, helpers parade and each is turned. The vyabhicāri is wonder that mere knowing proves wood-kind from afar. Proof by examples, relished.

essence: Sāṅkhya stated at full strength: pradhāna proved by presence, purposed by denying self-aims; change easy; only striving moves; nature faces down (vv19-22).
The page turns on admitted karma: where is His business? Let His triggering be conceived; seed imaged; Sāṅkhya godless; conditional close (vv23-27).

sections.SUMMARY: Sāṅkhya's pradhāna is proved by presence, purposed to spirit by denying self-aims; change comes easy again and again for enjoyment. Only person-aim-striving moves ever-maturing primal stuff; own-nature faces downward from root-cause-seeing toward body's ordaining. Karma admitted as possible mover — then the page turns: where is Īśvara's business? Let His change-triggering be conceived for root-nature's rangers. Seed-kitchens need nothing else, as in sprouts. Three-natured pradhāna leaves Sāṅkhya godless. Puruṣārtha-natured acts are conceived efficient by pradhāna.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as Sāṅkhya is stated fairly then outflanked by a question
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: the opponent at full strength, then the page turning on one question — where is His business? The vyabhicāri is admiration for fairness before victory. Debate relished.

essence: Potter necessary, nature watching, helpers insufficient, wisdom and will required, sufficiency tested (vv28-33).
Array excels by ends; Lord and un-Lord fenced off atomically; pradhāna will-less yet person-aim-ness stands (vv34-36).

sections.SUMMARY: Without that, no pot without a potter — how else? From clay-lump nature, own-nature watches potters. Entering matter with helpers never arrays — able though they be. Wisdom linked to world-traffic: never without. No will, no wonders — mere gross, never world-good. Rule-marvels only if mere potter-help bore pots. Never bodies otherwise — end-led array excels. Neither Lord nor un-Lord atomically taken — yet need fulfilled. Pradhāna will-less — person-aim-ness stands.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as each maker-candidate is tried and array excels
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: potter needed, helpers failing, will required, ends leading. The vyabhicāri is admiration for ends-first reasoning. Disputation relished.

essence: Unperceived buddhi grounds no purpose; generic will forces omniscience on each; perception-by-all mixes appearances unless One holds them (vv37-41).
Nature's kit needs no purpose and purpose is courtesy-speech — yet the root-cause would never cease, so no liberation without a perceiving maker (vv42-45).

sections.SUMMARY: Since intellect's arising stands unperceived by any spirit, no purpose follows — unspeakable, of spirit or of nature, though mind's motions come conditioned each in private ways. Will — how serve every soul? Give it to nature-in-general, and every soul turns all-knowing. One light would mix all shinings unless some One, in all undivided, keeps each apart. No world-plan makes seed put forth sprout; blind nature, kit and cause, brings green about — the wise join part to part, calling it spirit's purpose by courtesy. Granted — still, when purpose ends, the Root would churn its effects and never cease: sevenfold nature grants no release.

rasa.dominant: raudra-adbhuta of reductio pressed to the turn
rasa.sthayibhava: vitarka (reasoning-press) as each escape collapses into consequence
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is reasoning-press: unperceived will failing, generic will exploding into omniscience, nature-alone churning without release. The vyabhicāri is astonishment at the One undivided holding all spirits. Press relished.

essence: The svabhāva-view's consequences pressed: desired-by-all yet body-changes by nature; occurrence without union; needlessness fitting neither spirit nor mind; no reunion yet rebirth; mokṣa collapsed into nature; compassion-acts forcing passion-exhaustion doctrine (vv46-51).
The siddhānta sealed: nature-view abandoned as unjust, bodies famously sentient-maker-prior, arrangement-difference the flawless proof, the hetu aimed at Parameśvara unshaken (vv52-54).

sections.SUMMARY: From change, that One is longed for by all spirits — yet body's change runs by nature. As before, why not for the deemed-freed? It occurs, yet joins him not. Done and need-free he stands alone — yet needlessness fits no spirit ever, nor mind. With need gone, no meeting again — yet minds are born in bodies still. If sense-bound nature, not karma's waning, mokṣa is mere nature on karma's prop. Knowers act from compassion — yet passionless, release is passion's waning. Drop the nature-view, unjust; bodies bespeak a knowing Maker. From patterned difference, flawless proof — laid on the Lord by self-entrusted hand, unshaken.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as each consequence collapses and the maker stands
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: freed-spirit tests failing, mokṣa-into-nature absurd, compassion betraying passion — then abandonment, proof, aim. Triumph relished.

essence: Proof needs fitness: thousand-proved, it fails the deluded; the palm-held Jewel flees the fate-struck (v55). Self flashes as Īśvara within all breathers, maker and knower; recognition to be effected, joining made elsewhere; the proof stands even in duality — midnight fire (v56).

sections.SUMMARY: A thousand blazing reasons prove — yet not for minds astray; palm-held Maheśvara flees the fated, Jewel slipping away. Your own Self flashes — Īśvara in every breather's heart, Maker and Knower — yet Recognition stands apart; we wrought its joining elsewhere, and in duality too it stands — fit, and fuller: midnight fire burns brighter in our hands.

rasa.sthayibhava: vismaya (wonder) that proof flees the fated yet Self shines within all
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is wonder: thousand-proved yet ungrasped, palm-held yet fled — and Self flashing within every breather, midnight fire. Closing marvel relished.

lines: If mind's arising stands unmarked by any spirit's eye,
then 'for the spirit's sake' rings hollow — no purpose holds.
Of spirit, of nature — unspeakable, the mere word stays;
yet mind's own motions come conditioned, each in private ways.
Will — how could it serve the purposes of every soul?
Give it to nature-in-general, for all, to make it whole?
Unfelt by spirit, whose is will — and felt, then known by whom?
By all — then every soul is all-knowing: see where that must go.
One light would mix all separate shinings into one,
unless some One, in all undivided, keeps each apart — the turn begun.
No world-plan makes the seed put forth the sprout;
blind nature — kit and cause — brings green about.
What comes, well-formed — the wise join part to part;
we call it spirit's purpose — but by courtesy's art.
Say granted — still, when purpose ends, before the freed soul's face,
what stops the churn? The question hangs, demanding place.

lines: If mind is sense-bound nature, not freed by karma's cease,
release is nature itself — on karma's lease.

Drop the nature-view — unjust, unfit to stay;
bodies bespeak a knowing Maker, proved and plain as day.
From patterned difference — this stands, flawless proof;
no fault of reason touches it: here rests the truth.
This reason, laid upon the Lord by self-entrusted hand,
no fault of logic shakes — nor rival's: this shall stand.

lines: A thousand blazing reasons prove — yet not for minds astray;
palm-held Maheśvara flees the fated: Jewel slips away.
Your own Self flashes — Īśvara, in every breather's heart,
Maker and Knower — yet Recognition stands apart;
we wrought its joining elsewhere; in duality too it stands —
fit, and fuller: midnight fire burns brighter in our hands.
Who makes — him, I praise,
the one God, Maheśvara the Lord.
Bodies and the rest have conscious cause,
distinct-arrayed — pots … like atoms.
notes: mid-verse gap kept visible (…); atoms-pot pairing partly lost

lines: Conscious-urged — or …
[…] as pot from [tha]t.
notes: lacuna-fragment: gaps kept visible (…), nothing restored

lines: … devoid of locus-form. Fixed,
its meaning stands in place — in that action-heaped …
notes: lacuna-fragment: gaps kept visible (…), nothing restored

lines: Amid the varied, mind alone stands clear —
pots prove it: the wise Maker means each form for use.
isva-p01-v05.sanskrit_cite: vicitre buddhimāneva ghaṭādiṣviva lakṣyate kartā vijño vicitraitadupayogābhisaṃdhimān

lines: There is, in function-yoking, among bodies and worlds,
this distinct array — never from mere matter.
Here then — conscious makers proved, the Lord's act proved:
for knowers of such variety, no lordlessness could be.
isva-p01-v07.sanskrit_cite: tadatra buddhimatkartṛsiddhyā siddheśvarakriyā na hi tādṛśavaicitryaviduṣaḥ syādanīśitā

lines: Neither potter nor Lord shows agreement here —
since for him, contradiction would follow — or else unproved accord.
isva-p01-v08.sanskrit_cite: na kulālena neśenāpyanvayo'tra pradarśyate yato viruddhatāsya syādasiddhānvayatāpi vā

lines: Merely showing pervasion with the conscious alone —
by thesis-force, somewhere, someone wise is understood.
As combination seen for others' sake alone —
in eye and the rest, by that fitness: the self-dear, uncompounded higher.
isva-p02-v10.sanskrit_cite: yathā pārārthyamātreṇa saṃghātatve'nvitekṣite cakṣurādau tadaucityādātmeṣṭo'saṃhataḥ paraḥ

lines: As from afar, from smoke, proof comes in the khadira grove —
fire stands proved by knowing it: as khadira-wood.
isva-p02-v11.sanskrit_cite: yathā vā dūrato dhūmātsiddhiḥ khadirakānane vahnistatpratipattyaiva khādiratvena siddhyati

lines: So the cause: bare locus-form, here set apart —
not by mere variety, nor as particular's mark.
isva-p02-v12.sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ca hetuḥ saṃsthānamātramatra viśeṣitam tathā vaicitryamātreṇa na svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā

lines: By others too, sifting reasons in the pot's self-proving —
bare locus-form … even … causehood of the conscious.
isva-p02-v13.sanskrit_cite: paraistairapi hetūnāṃ ghaṭātmapravivecane saṃsthānamātra eva............ hetutvaṃ buddhiśālinaḥ
notes: mid-verse gap kept visible (…); nothing restored

lines: Shaped for mutual use, locus-formed — that whole world, this —
rightly Lord-made.
Here is the reply: a strange way of helpers is seen —
some would join with stuff, somehow — a joining.
isva-p02-v15.sanskrit_cite: atrocyate gatiścitrā dṛśyate sahakāriṇām kecitkathaṃcideveyurupādānaiḥ samāgamam

lines: Helpers, entering as others, reaching matter's shape —
picture effects indeed — like earth-and-water saps.
isva-p02-v16.sanskrit_cite: hetumantaḥpraviśyānye prāpyopādānarūpatām citrayanti hi kāryāṇi bhaumodakarasā iva

lines: Others again, in matter, outward-bent —
unequal to yoking varied form in effects.
isva-p02-v17.sanskrit_cite: anye punarupādāne bahirviparivartinaḥ rūpavaicitryayogāya kāryeṣu na tathā kṣamāḥ

lines: There, if the conscious one's spread be fancied in name —
yet not by that alone does order hold everywhere.
isva-p02-v18.sanskrit_cite: tatra buddhimato nāma prasaro yadi kalpyate na tāvataiva sarvatra vyavasthā ghaṭate tathā

lines: Pradhāna stands proved there, by presence and the rest —
denying self-aims and their kin, person-aim-ness stands proved.
isva-p03-v19.sanskrit_cite: asti cāsya pradhānasya prasiddhasyānvayādinā svārthatādiniṣedhena sādhitā puruṣārthatā

lines: Through that, proving spirit's joy again and again —
no change would be hard at all.
isva-p03-v20.sanskrit_cite: tenāsya bhogasaṃsiddhiḥ puruṣasya yathā yathā tathā tathā pariṇatiḥ syānna kiṃcana durghaṭam

lines: Hence indeed, for ever-becoming pradhāna, no mover
but person-aim-striving.
isva-p03-v21.sanskrit_cite: ata eva pradhānasya mahattvapariṇāminaḥ nimittakāraṇaṃ nānyatpuruṣārthodyamādṛte

lines: Own-nature indeed — and this of this — from root-cause-seeing on;
below mind-ground, toward the body's ordaining.
isva-p03-v22.sanskrit_cite: svabhāva eva caiṣo'sya mūlahetostathekṣaṇāt cittabhūmeradharataḥ śarīrādividhiṃ prati
notes: tatekṣaṇāt both parses equivalent in force

lines: As mover, karma could be primal-natured even.
Then here — where is Īśvara's work to be conceived?
isva-p03-v23.sanskrit_cite: nimittakāraṇaṃ karma syādapyādyasvabhāvataḥ tato'tra kutra vyāpāra īśvarasyopakalpyatām

lines: Warding the inner rangers in root-nature, of secret kind —
let Īśvara be thought change-trigger.
If of one-change-nature — then thence:
a beholden-to-none seed-kit, as in sprouts.
isva-p03-v25.sanskrit_cite: yadyathā pariṇāmaikasvabhāvaṃ tatra tattataḥ ananyāpekṣi bījādisāmagrī yadvadaṅkure

lines: Mahat-led, torrent-like in change, triple-stranded root self —
and thereby: godless Sāṅkhya.
isva-p03-v26.sanskrit_cite: mahadādivikāraughapariṇāmasvabhāvakam triguṇātma pradhānaṃ ca tena sāṃkhyamanīśvaram

lines: If purposed for spirit in every act it works —
primal stuff is deemed its mover.
Without that — without a potter —
how could there even be a pot?
From the clay-lump made of pradhāna, such-natured by nature —
own-nature now, this of this, watching the potter.
isva-p04-v29.sanskrit_cite: pradhānamayamṛtpiṇḍādeva tādṛksvabhāvataḥ atha svabhāva eṣo'sya yatkulālādyapekṣaṇam

lines: Never — by entering matter's inside with helpers —
could array be wrought — able though they be.
isva-p04-v30.sanskrit_cite: naivopādanahetvantaḥ praveśātsahakāribhiḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣo'pi śakyaḥ kartumiti kṣamam

lines: World-traffic-linked wisdom —
without — never.
notes: hemistich as printed (cd lost); nothing restored

lines: So with no will to make, no wonders made —
mere grossness would be, never world-good.
isva-p04-v32.sanskrit_cite: tathā cikīrṣāṃ ca vinā vicitraracanodbhavaḥ sthūlatāmātrameva syānna tu lokopayoginī

lines: Ruled making would be marvelous in kind —
if mere potter-help bore pots.
isva-p04-v33.sanskrit_cite: racanā niyamena syādvicitrā jātirūpiṇī kulālasahakāritvamātrāccejjāyate ghaṭaḥ

lines: Never bodies and the rest — long clay-lump or … —
hence array excels, end-led.
isva-p04-v34.sanskrit_cite: na syājjātu śarīrādi dīrghamṛtpiṇḍa eva vā ata evārthanīyatvātsaṃniveśo viśiṣyate

lines: He stands proved not by pot-ness but by answered need;
no Lord, no un-Lord takes the atomic mark indeed.
isva-p04-v35.sanskrit_cite: na ghaṭāditayā siddhaḥ so'rthitāparipūrakaḥ na ceśvaro'nīśvaro vā prakṛto'trāṇulakṣaṇaḥ

lines: No desire-arising of primal stuff —
person-aim-ness stands.
notes: na-scope held open (fencing will vs denying aims)

lines: If mind's arising stands unmarked by any spirit's eye,
then 'for the spirit's sake' rings hollow — no purpose holds.
Of spirit, of nature — unspeakable, the mere word stays;
yet mind's own motions come conditioned, each in private ways.
Will — how could it serve the purposes of every soul?
Give it to nature-in-general, for all, to make it whole?
Unfelt by spirit, whose is will — and felt, then known by whom?
By all — then every soul is all-knowing: see where that must go.
One light would mix all separate shinings into one,
unless some One, in all undivided, keeps each apart — the turn begun.
No world-plan makes the seed put forth the sprout;
blind nature — kit and cause — brings green about.
What comes, well-formed — the wise join part to part;
we call it spirit's purpose — but by courtesy's art.
Say granted — still, when purpose ends, before the freed soul's face,
what stops the churn? The question hangs, demanding place.
isva-p05-v44.sanskrit_cite: iti cet tatsamāptau api puruṣārthe api taṃ prati

lines: The Root would churn its own effects and never cease;
oh, never — sevenfold nature grants no release!
isva-p05-v45.sanskrit_cite: na viramen mūlakāraṇam āho na viramati

lines: From change, all spirits long for that changeless One;
yet body's change, earth's change, runs by nature on.
isva-p06-v46.sanskrit_cite: pariṇāmāt tad ekaṃ hi sarvān puṃsaḥ pratīṣyate

lines: Why not, as before, for him deemed freed of need?
It still occurs — yet joins him not.
isva-p06-v47.sanskrit_cite: pūrvavan na bhavet kasmāt taṃ muktābhimataṃ prati

lines: Done and need-free, the freed soul stands alone, you say;
yet needlessness fits spirit never — nor mind's sway.
Once need is gone, no meeting with the soul again;
yet minds are born in bodies still — the claim is vain.
isva-p06-v49.sanskrit_cite: arthitvavigamān na syād bhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ

release is nature itself — on karma's lease.
